about: Research sheet for the Kansas county edition. Every contact below was read on the date in reviewed_on from the page named beside it; scripts/make_county_state.py turns it into the edition files.
name: Kansas
phones_sentence: Kansas has no county veterans offices. Field office phones, addresses, counties and itinerant schedules come from each office’s page on the Kansas Office of Veterans Services website. Call before you go.

offices.source_title: Kansas Office of Veterans Services: KOVS VSR and VSO Office Locations
offices.note: Kansas Office of Veterans Services veteran service representatives help with VA claims, pension, survivor benefits and appeals at no charge. Itinerant travel and appointments are subject to change; call before you go.
offices.selection: Field office address and phones as printed on the office’s page on the Kansas Office of Veterans Services website, with its itinerant schedule for the county; staff names, emails and fax numbers omitted.

programs.name: Kansas veterans: state field offices for claims help
programs.description: Free help with VA claims, appeals, pension and survivor benefits from Kansas Office of Veterans Services veteran service representatives. Kansas has no county veterans offices: 16 state field offices, from Colby to Kansas City, each serve a set of counties, and most hold monthly itinerant hours in nearby towns.
programs.next_step: Choose your county for its field office and itinerant schedule, and call the office to schedule an appointment. The department’s toll-free line is 800-513-7731.
constraints: Itinerant visits and appointments are subject to change; call before you go.
The Winfield office’s representative position is vacant; its counties are asked to call the eastern-region supervisor.

programs.description: Kansas’s Aging and Disability Resource Center is a statewide call center that helps older adults, people with disabilities and caregivers find long-term care options and in-home and community services, and can complete the assessment needed before nursing facility admission. Local Area Agencies on Aging serve as its regional offices. Military service is not required.
programs.next_step: Call 855-200-2372 (855-200-ADRC), Monday–Friday 8 a.m.–5 p.m.; you can leave a message after hours. Or choose a county above for its Area Agency on Aging.
constraints: Each program has its own eligibility and waitlist.

programs.name: Kansas Long-Term Care Ombudsman and adult abuse reporting
programs.organization: Kansas Office of the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman
programs.description: Independent advocacy for residents of nursing homes, assisted living and other adult care homes, through regional ombudsmen and the state office in Topeka.
programs.next_step: Call the state ombudsman office at 877-662-8362 (785-296-3017), or choose a county above for its regional ombudsman. To report abuse, neglect or exploitation of an adult, call the Kansas Protection Report Center at 800-922-5330, 24 hours a day. To report abuse, neglect or poor care in a nursing home or other licensed adult care home, call the KDADS complaint hotline at 800-842-0078. In an emergency, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing agency.

programs.name: Free legal help for Kansas veterans and older adults
programs.description: Kansas Legal Services gives civil legal help across the state from offices in Dodge City, Emporia, Hays, Hutchinson, Kansas City, Manhattan, Pittsburg, Salina, Seneca, Topeka and Wichita. Its Elder Law Hotline connects Kansans 60 and older with volunteer attorneys who answer civil legal questions at no charge.
programs.next_step: Apply online, or call the Kansas Legal Services application line at 800-723-6953 (statewide client intake: 316-267-3975). If you are 60 or older, call the Elder Law Hotline at 888-353-5337, Monday–Friday 9 a.m.–4:30 p.m.
constraints: Legal aid screens by income and case type.
The Elder Law Hotline answers civil questions only; it can also refer you to private attorneys, who charge for their services.

programs.name: VA health care systems serving Kansas
programs.description: Kansas veterans are served mainly by VA Wichita health care (Robert J. Dole VA Medical Center, 5500 East Kellogg Drive, Wichita; 316-685-2221), which serves 59 Kansas counties, and the VA Eastern Kansas Healthcare System (Colmery-O’Neil VA Medical Center, 2200 SW Gage Boulevard, Topeka, 785-350-3111 or 800-574-8387; and the Dwight D. Eisenhower VA Medical Center in Leavenworth). VA Kansas City health care (Kansas City VA Medical Center, Missouri; 816-861-4700) also has a clinic in Overland Park.
programs.next_step: Use VA’s facility locator with your ZIP code to find the closest clinic. Not enrolled yet? Ask your Kansas Office of Veterans Services field office for help applying.
constraints: Which system serves you depends on where you live; VA’s locator shows the right clinic.

All 105 counties also show an Area Agency on Aging (eleven), a regional long-term care ombudsman and a Center for Independent Living (eight centers).
